Question: Call a positive integer an uphill integer if every digit is strictly greater than the previous digit. For example, \(1357,\) \(89,\) and \(5\) are all uphill integers, but \(32,\) \(1240,\) and \(466\) are not. How many uphill integers are divisible by \(15?\)
